::: {.why}
Every statistic this week is estimated from a sample that mostly does not contain the event you are worried about, and a stress test is the honest response to that rather than a compliance exercise.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report your book's performance in three historical stress windows and say which exposure drove each result.
- Construct one hypothetical scenario that is not in your sample and defend the size of the shocks you chose.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Run the historical scenarios: your current book's weights held through October 2008, March 2020 and your third episode, with the factor exposures decomposed so you can attribute the loss rather than only report it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Build one hypothetical: pick a correlation and volatility configuration that has not occurred in your sample but is not physically impossible, such as your two strategies becoming correlated at 0.8 while volatility triples. Report the loss and say what would have to be true in the world for it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the results into reports/milestone-04-risk-model.md with the attribution, not just the numbers.
:::
:::
